newsitem.title: Usa: In victory, Clinton urges cooperation with Congress.
newsitem.headline: In victory, Clinton urges cooperation with Congress.

text.p: President Bill Clinton, in a low key, formal victory speech, said the American people had sent a message with their votes that the Democratic president and Republican Congress must work together.

In a ceremony attended by thousands of supporters outside the white-pillared Arkansas State House, Clinton paid tribute to his Republican opponent Bob Dole, asking the crowd to join him in applauding the former Senate leader's "lifetime of service to the United States." He said: "I wish him well and God speed."

Clinton, in a subdued speech that contrasted with the exuberance of the victory rally after his 1992 win, made clear he had no illusions about the problems he will face dealing with a Congress that remains narrowly under Republican control after Tuesday's vote.
By returning a closely divided Congress, the American people were "sending us a message. Work together, meet our challenges," Clinton said. "When we join our hands ... America always wins."

Commentators expect the Republicans to hammer home the attacks on Clinton that have characterised the closing stages of the election campaign, pushing calls for investigations of questionable Democratic fund-raising and Clinton's links to a series of scandals known collectively as Whitewater. He addressed one of those areas in his speech, calling on all sides to work on reforming campaign financing. "I am willing to act and ask others to join me," he said.

Clinton said he had spoken with Dole by telephone during the evening. "I thanked him for his love of our country, for his years of service. I applauded the campaign he fought so bravely until the very last minute. I thanked him for the work we did together to advance the common cause of America..."
